6-Generation Pedigree Analysis

Map your family cancer history across great-great-grandparents to children. Our AI detects hereditary patterns and autosomal dominant inheritance.

Genetic Mutation Modeling

Analyzes BRCA1, BRCA2, TP53, KRAS, HER2 and 20+ more genes. Models missense, nonsense, and frameshift mutations with penetrance probability.

Combines smoking history, BMI, diet, stress, pollution exposure and more to model DNA methylation effects and chronic inflammation risk.

Voice-Assisted Interaction

Speak to fill forms, ask questions, and hear results explained aloud. Adapts tone by age — warm & encouraging for kids, professional for adults.

AI Chat Assistant

Upload medical reports and get them explained in simple language. Personalized guidance, screening reminders, and emotional support messages.

Patient Support Module

Stage-based guidance, nutrition suggestions, pain management tips, and motivational success stories for those already diagnosed with cancer.

🛡️

Privacy & Ethical Safety

All genetic data is encrypted. System always shows disclaimer — this is awareness, not diagnosis. Avoids fear-based messaging at all times.

Tumor Awareness Module

Learn about benign vs malignant tumors, TNM staging, oncogenes, and tumor suppressor genes explained at your chosen comprehension level.

    🔬 Tumor Awareness Module
    Understanding tumors — explained at your level
    🟢

    Benign Tumors (Non-Cancerous)

    Slow growing, well-defined borders, do not spread to other tissues. Usually surgically removable. Examples include Lipoma, Fibroadenoma, and Adenoma.

    Slow growth No spreading Often curable
    🔴

    Malignant Tumors (Cancerous)

    Rapid growth, invade nearby tissue, can metastasize (spread to distant organs). Require comprehensive medical treatment including surgery, chemo, or radiation.

    Rapid growth Can spread Invasive
    🏥 TNM Staging System
    T
    Tumor Size
    A gene mutation means a small change in your body's instruction system. T refers to how large the primary tumor has grown.
    N
    Node Involvement
    N describes whether cancer has reached nearby lymph nodes — part of your immune system.
    M
    Metastasis
    M indicates whether the cancer has spread to distant parts of the body like lungs, liver, or bones.
    🧬 Key Cancer Genes
    🚨

    Oncogenes (Accelerators)

    When mutated, these genes cause uncontrolled cell growth.

    KRAS HER2 MYC BRAF
    🛡️

    Tumor Suppressor Genes

    Normally stop cancer — when lost, cancer can develop.

    TP53 BRCA1 BRCA2 APC PTEN

    You Are Stronger Than Cancer

    "Every day is a new chance to fight."

    Thousands of people around the world are beating cancer every single day. Modern medicine, early detection, and a strong support system make all the difference.

    🥗 Cancer-Fighting Nutrition Guide
    🥦

    Cruciferous Vegetables

    Broccoli, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts — rich in sulforaphane, shown to inhibit tumor growth and support cellular repair.

    🫐

    Antioxidant-Rich Berries

    Blueberries, strawberries, raspberries contain anthocyanins that fight oxidative stress and inflammation linked to cancer.

    🐟

    Omega-3 Rich Foods

    Salmon, sardines, flaxseeds provide anti-inflammatory omega-3 fatty acids that may reduce cancer risk and support treatment.

    🫚

    Turmeric & Spices

    Curcumin in turmeric has demonstrated anti-tumor properties in numerous studies. Best absorbed with black pepper.
